subject: Tenant bridge + egress policy runbook — architecture review request
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant bridge + egress policy runbook — architecture review request

Hi team,

Attaching the latest draft of the tenant-bridge reference diagram and the first pass of the tenant egress runbook for Aurora Health. We need a quick technical review focused on the control-plane/data-plane separation and the proposed egress behaviour for tenant traffic that will route through their appliance cluster.

Quick summary: 
- Goal: Support Aurora's private deployment with a split control/data plane. Control plane (managed) remains in our VPC; data plane lives in Aurora's colo racks.
- Tenant bridge: east-west NAT gateway + BGP peer to Aurora leafs for control-plane telemetry and service discovery.
- Egress: preference for SNAT at tenant NAT for auditability; fallback to centralized egress (our egress-proxy) if tenant environment cannot meet firewall policy.

Attachments: vpc-tenant-bridge-diagram-v3.pdf (pdf), tenant-egress-policy-runbook-draft.md (markdown)

Asks: 
1) Jonas — can you validate the BGP adjacency and whether using a /31 peer is acceptable for Aurora's fabric?
2) Marissa — any concerns about KV cache replication over the peered link (latency/consistency)?
3) Kimberly — please confirm the audit log surface we need to request from Aurora for retention and export (SOC2 evidence).

Deadline: I'd like feedback by end-of-day Thursday (26th) so we can consolidate and send to Aurora before their security review meeting next week.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant bridge + egress policy runbook — architecture review request

Avery — thanks for the doc and diagrams. Quick notes inline (high level):

- BGP peering: /31 is fine for a dedicated point-to-point between our edge router and Aurora leafs, but confirm their router OS supports /31s for RFC 3021. If not, fall back to /30. Also call out the expected ASNs and a preferred BFD interval for failover (we recommend 300ms).

- KV cache replication: The diagram shows a synchronous replication over the tenant uplink. Recommend changing to async with strong read-after-write guarantees for control-plane metadata only. Synchronous replication across a WAN increases tail latency and will impact small-token latency for generation requests.

- Egress approach: SNAT at the tenant NAT is preferred for visibility, but we need a clear fallback for tenants who cannot provide per-tenant NAT address ranges (some colos are unwilling). Add a section in the runbook that defines the order of precedence: (1) Tenant SNAT; (2) Tenant routed /30 with NAT on our egress-proxy; (3) Encrypted tunnel to our central egress-proxy with tenant tags.

- Audit logs: we need: flow logs (VPC and border), per-request correlation id injected in the control-plane headers, and Kafka topic retention policy (30 days by default). Kimberly — please confirm whether 30 days meets Aurora's compliance; if they require 90+ we need a costs note.

I made a few redlines in the runbook doc (see attachment: tenant-egress-policy-runbook-draft.md) and annotated the diagram with alternate peering options. 

If Jonas can answer the BGP/MTU questions by EOD, I'll consolidate and send to Aurora.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Miranda Lee <miranda.lee@aurorahealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Networking <ops@aurorahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant bridge + egress policy runbook — architecture review request

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from our networking team: 

1) We do support /31s on our Juniper aggregation routers but need to confirm whether Redwood expects BFD. We prefer not to enable aggressive BFD timers.
2) For the audit log retention, our compliance team asks for 90 days for border flow logs; 30 days is not sufficient. Can Redwood handle a 90-day retention for Aurora-specific topics (we can pay incremental storage).
3) On SNAT: some of our colos use NAT64/64 pools and cannot provide stable public SNAT IPs per tenant. We would need the centralized egress-proxy option.

We can do a 45-minute walkthrough next Monday (Nov 29) at 10:00 AM PT to go over hit points.

Attaching our internal network constraints doc: aurora-net-constraints.pdf (small)

Thanks,
Miranda Lee
Lead Network Engineer — Aurora Health
miranda.lee@aurorahealth.com
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Miranda Lee <miranda.lee@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant bridge + egress policy runbook — architecture review request

Miranda — thanks for the details, that all makes sense. Short responses and next steps below: 

1) BFD — we will not enforce aggressive BFD by default. We'll publish recommended timers in the runbook and leave BFD optional. Jonas: I'll follow up to add a note recommending 1s/3s timers as a conservative default.

2) Retention — 90 days is fine for Aurora-specific topics. Kimberly, please prepare an alternative retention-cost estimate and we will include it in the commercial note.

3) SNAT / Centralized egress — accept the constraint. We'll add a fallback flow that routes tenant egress traffic via an encrypted tunnel to our central egress-proxy and annotate the diagram. We'll also call out the per-tenant tagging and correlation-id propagation for logs.

Action items: 
- Jonas: confirm MTU and /31 compatibility and add BGP examples to JIRA-INF-4821 (due: Mon EOD).
- Kimberly: cost for 90-day retention and SOC2 evidence checklist to include (due: Mon EOD).
- Marissa: final runbook consolidation and send to Aurora before the Nov 29 walkthrough (due: Mon morning).

I'll schedule the Nov 29 10:00 AM PT walkthrough and invite the Aurora networking team; calendar invite to follow.

Thanks all — will update the diagram and push a v3.1 to the shared Drive link.

Best,
Avery
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
